collectible:1.text: Tags are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 100 Tags located all around Los Santos, which the player must find and paint a Grove Street Families tag over it using a Spray Can while on foot. A tag needs at least 29 units of Spray Can "ammo" to be completely sprayed over.

collectible:2.text: Snapshots are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 50 Snapshots located all around San Fierro and city limits, which the player must find and photograph using a Camera. The Camera has several spawn points in San Fierro, all located near Snapshot locations.

collectible:3.text: Horseshoes are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 50 Horseshoes located all around Las Venturas, which the player must find and collect while on foot. Each Horseshoe collected rewards the player with $100 and 20 points of "Luck" in the Stats menu (which does not affect the gameplay in any way), totaling $5,000 and 1000 "Luck" points for collecting all Horseshoes.

collectible:4.text: Oysters are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 50 Oysters located all around San Andreas, which the player must find and collect while swimming. Each Oyster collected rewards the player with $100, totaling $5,000 for collecting all Oysters alone. Collecting all 50 Oysters is a requirement for the 100% completion.

collectible:5.text: Unique Stunt Jumps (also known as Unique Jumps in 3D Universe and Stunt Jumps in GTA IV) are a feature in every Grand Theft Auto game since GTA III (with the exception of GTA Advance). All GTA games have jumps set up around their maps for "insane" stunting.

easter-egg:2.text: Catalina is the main antagonist of Grand Theft Auto III and a major character in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Catalina was a criminal in Red County in GTA San Andreas and the leader of the Colombian Cartel in GTA III. She is the cousin of Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando. Catalina is of mixed Dominican and Colombian descent.

easter-egg:3.text: The Gant Bridge is a suspension bridge in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It is part of the Las Venturas Highway connecting San Fierro with Las Venturas. Gant Bridge is an iconic landmark of San Fierro, San Andreas, connecting Juniper Hollow and Palisades in San Fierro to Tierra Robada and Bayside. Spanning San Fierro Bay, the bridge also serves as the western gateway to the waterways which divide San Andreas state.

easter-egg:4.text: The Hidden Sign is an Easter egg in Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories left by the designers for the player to find. Located in a remote alley around a parking lot in Staunton Island, it is a large message written in black on a white rectangular board propped against a wall.

easter-egg:5.text: The Mass Grave is a pit located at the foot of a mesa in El Castillo del Diablo, Bone County, northwest of Area 69, southwest of the Verdant Meadows Airfield and just across the street from the Snake Farm in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The pit, which takes the form of a large round hole, contains six body bags, and a Bobcat truck next to the pit.

easter-egg:6.text: Scott Wilson is a character who is mentioned in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Wilson died either during or some time prior to 1992, the year of the game's setting. He is buried at the Drive-Thru Confessions Church in Palomino Creek, Red County.

easter-egg:7.text: Caligula's Palace (also known as Caligula's Casino) is a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas, in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It is situated between The Clown's Pocket and Royal Casino. According to the game manual, it houses the largest hotel in the world. It is owned by the Sindacco Crime Family, but later shared between them and the Leone Crime Family and Forelli Crime Family.

easter-egg:8.text: Clothing U.S.A is a chain of discount clothing stores in Grand Theft Auto IV and Episodes from Liberty City. The business is a rendition of a now-closed, unnamed store that was located at 224 Market Street in Newark, New Jersey.

easter-egg:9.text: The Parachute is an item that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, The Ballad of Gay Tony, Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online. In The Ballad of Gay Tony, it is manufactured by ProLaps. The Parachute is designed for only one purpose in the games it appears in: to safely return the player to ground level after falling from a significant height.

easter-egg:10.text: The San Fierro Tower, also known as Downtown skyscraper, is an unnamed building in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It is tallest building in San Fierro and the second tallest building in the State of San Andreas. It is located in Downtown, beside the entrance to the Garver Bridge. Its footprint is triangular in shape, and it has an open space cut through it, which is a very unique feature.

easter-egg:11.text: Waning with the Stars is a reality show that is advertised as appearing on Weazel in Grand Theft Auto IV; however, it is not a viewable program on the in-game television.

easter-egg:12.text: Zero RC is a hobby shop operated by RC hobbyist and electronics expert Zero in Garcia, San Fierro featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The shop is owned by an unnamed landlord up until 1992, when the landlord decides to sell the shop. Zero has been living above the shop and fears that he would be evicted once the shop is sold. In desperation, Zero calls Carl Johnson pleading for help.

easter-egg:13.text: Carcer Gas is a brand of propane from Carcer City that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, originating from the Manhunt series. Tanks containing the propane can be seen at various locations through San Andreas, primarily at gas stations and a trailer park on the Flint Intersection. Some Waltons can also be seen carrying tanks on their beds.

easter-egg:15.text: The Hydra is a military VTOL attack jet featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the Heists update. It is the first military jet available in the Grand Theft Auto series. It is manufactured by Mammoth in the HD Universe.

easter-egg:16.text: Manhunt is a stealth, horror-survival videogame duology developed by Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games. The first game, Manhunt, was originally released for the PlayStation 2 on November 18, 2003.

easter-egg:18.text: Northstar Rock is a small area in Red County, San Andreas, located north of Los Santos, that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The area is named "Northstar Rock" on the map included with the game; however, on the in-game map, this area is named North Rock.

easter-egg:22.text: Denise Robinson's House is the home of Denise Robinson in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Denise's house is located near Grove Street in Ganton, Los Santos. After the mission Burning Desire for C.R.A.S.H., protagonist Carl Johnson can date Denise by picking her up from her home. A green Hustler is often parked in front of the house, which can be accessed after Carl's relationship with Denise reaches 50%.

easter-egg:24.text: GoPostal is the official postal courier delivery service in Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto Online and Grand Theft Auto VI. The player can buy stocks from the company on the LCN Exchange website. It is one of the two main delivery companies in the game, the other being Post OP. The owner of the company and when it was founded is unknown.

easter-egg:27.text: The James Bomb is a sports car in Grand Theft Auto: London 1969. The James Bomb is a hardtop coupe-styled sports car available only in gray, suggestively based on the Aston Martin DB5. Obviously enough, its name is a play of on "James Bond", a prominent fictional spy from a series of espionage novels, which in turn spawned a decades old movie series first produced during the 1960s.
